LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. Based on how the odds are looking heading into this contest , many are expecting the night to be a bit one-sided in the hands of the Texans on their home field on a short week. But as with any divisional matchup in the NFL, there's always bound to be some unexpected surprises to unfold that make the events pan out a bit differently than the general consensus expects. With that in mind, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions on how Thursday night's action could look between the Texans and Colts: Daniel Jones Throws Three Interceptions Sep 27, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) drops back to pass against the Houston Texans in the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Texans have seen firsthand just how ugly things can get for the Colts and their offense when Daniel Jones is feeling turnover-happy. In their Week 3 matchup, it was Jones who gave up three turnovers between two interceptions and a fumble, and still managed to claw out a narrow 19-17 victory . The Texans have seen firsthand just how ugly things can get for the Colts and their offense when Daniel Jones is feeling turnover-happy. In their Week 3 matchup, it was Jones who gave up three turnovers between two interceptions and a fumble, and still managed to claw out a narrow 19-17 victory . It's hard to imagine the Texans winning the turnover battle 3-0 and still coming up short once again. On the other hand, it might not be too tough to picture Jones struggling with his ball security in another matchup against this defense, especially when factoring in a short week on the road without many reliable weapons in his arsenal of pass-catchers. On the season, Jones is averaging nearly two turnovers a game between his league-leading 12 interceptions and five fumbles. If the Texans take an early lead, and the game script forces the Colts to keep throwing the ball, the door could be wide open for Houston to capitalize on multiple errors from Indianapolis' signal-caller. Will Anderson Claims Three Sacks Jan 4, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson Jr. (51) reacts after a play during the game against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The stage feels like it's set for a monster game to come from Texans' All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. The stage feels like it's set for a monster game to come from Texans' All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. For one, the Texans are forced to enter this matchup without Danielle Hunter for the second straight game due to a hamstring injury. That means Houston will have to rely on Anderson to carry a bit more of the load within the pass-rush than usual–– but considering he leads the lead in total sacks through 10 weeks, we know he's more than capable of doing just that. On top of Hunter's absence, though, the Colts will be dealing with some key injuries on their offensive line to starting tackles Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis. So Anderson––one of the best pass-rushers the NFL has to offer––will have the opportunity to go up against a pair of backup tackles on the Colts line coming off a short week. Anderson has already had one game this season logging three sacks against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5, and maybe Indianapolis is the next AFC South opponent up to face that same fate on Thursday. Marvin Harrison Jr, wide receiver: Hamstring (projected to be OUT) Danielle Hunter, defensive end: Hamstring (projected to be OUT) Brevin Jordan, tight end: foot/illness (projected to be OUT) Woody Marks, running back: concussion (projected to be OUT) There are no real changes from Sunday afternoon. All the major injuries from before will keep the same crop of playmakers out on Thursday. However, the Colts are faced with a catastrophe of injuries that will ensure a skeleton crew approach on Amazon Prime. Sauce Gardner, cornerback: calf (projected to be Questionable) Anthony Gould, wide receiver: toe (projected to be Questionable) Charlie Heck, offensive tackle: personal (projected to be Questionable) Will Mallory, tight end: hamstring (projected to be OUT) Bernhard Raimann, offensive tackle: concussion (projected to be OUT) Luke Rhodes, longsnapper: hamstring (projected to be Questionable) Jerry Tillery, defensive tackle: calf (projected to be OUT) Jalen Travis, offensive tackle: knee (projected to be OUT) Charvarius Ward, cornerback: knee (projected to be OUT) On Houston's side, they're dealing with an injury slate the looks like: Kamari Lassiter, cornerback: wrist (reportedly in line to play) Houston Texans have significant injury advantage against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night On the Colts' side of things, things look much bleeker on the personnel front. After conducting a walk-through on Wednesday, their projected injury concerns are: By my count, that's two cornerbacks, one wide receiver, three offensive tackles, one tight end, one defensive tackle and even a longsnapper that have some type of designation before the contest. Thats after already not having the likes of DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, Alec Pierce Josh Downs and Quenton Nelson on the team at the moment due to either injury or trade offs at the NFL trade deadline. For all intents and purposes, Houston should absolutely roll over Indianapolis by at least 20 points. However, given the volatile—and deeply disturbing—performance tendencies of the home team over their first nine games, one would be wise to not put anything past them at this stage. The Colts have waved the white flag on the season, while the Texans—even at 3-6—are still very much mathematically alive in the AFC playoff race. Even still, fans at Reliant won't be holding their breath on a comfortable viewing experience. home.headline: Is Deshaun Watson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10)
home.blurb: Is Deshaun Watson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. The prop market projects Watson to threw for 207.5 passing yards while he's -273 to throw a touchdown and -123 to throw an interception. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Miami's offense played well enough under quarterback Kyle McCord, making his NFL debut after spending his rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad last year, and the defense did its part to keep Miami in the game. The special teams let down the Dolphins – with kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point during the game. The Dolphins' loss was yet another straight-up loss, but they did enough to cover the 3.5-point spread throughout the week, or the 4.5-point mark to which the spread ballooned on Sunday. Miami is being given an even bigger window for next week's game. Miami visits the Buffalo Bills in Week 11, the first of two meetings between the AFC East rivals in 2026. The win moved the Bills to 8-1 for the year and keeps them in the top spot in the AFC playoff picture, a game ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs and Jacksonville Jaguars. The winner of tonight's Sunday Night Football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will also reach the 7-2 mark, a game behind Buffalo. The Bills are -1800 on the moneyline for the straight-up victory, while the Dolphins are +980. The point total opened at 47.5. McCord will start his second game in Week 11, looking to continue to grow in the Dolphins' offense as he replaces Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve with a groin injury. McCord finished the game 17-for-32 for 209 yards with no touchdown passes or interceptions; he did score a rushing touchdown. The Dolphins face their AFC East rivals, the Buffalo Bills, on the road this weekend, a game that features a team tied for the worst record in the AFC visiting the team with the best record in the conference. Division games are typically closer than expected, but this one might be the exception that proves the rule. Miami is relying on rookies and first-year players across the roster this year, including quarterback Kyle McCord. picks.blurb: Buffalo Bills Predicted to Make Necessary Move on 11-Year Veteran Ahead of Dolphins Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Bills predicted to make necessary move on Tre'Davious White. Getty Cole Shelton · HEAVY Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. Getty The Buffalo Bills could rely on a veteran cornerback against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo is coming off a road win over the New York Jets to improve to 8-1 and is atop the AFC. The Bills have been playing great, but they did suffer some key injuries in the win, which could mean the team has to make some roster moves. Buffalo is set to host the Dolphins on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Predicted to Promote Tre'Davious White GettyBills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. In the Bills' win over the Jets, starting cornerback Christian Benford suffered an injury, which is a bit of a concern. However, if Benford can't go, Bills reporter Joe Buscagalia of The Athletic believes the team will elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscagalia wrote . "That's also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … "If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on." White would be entering his 11th NFL season. He signed with Buffalo's practice squad during the year as he wanted to return after starting 16 games and playing well a year ago. Buffalo selected White in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a lockdown corner. Although he's no longer the No. 1 cornerback he once was, he can add some depth to the cornerback room if Benford is out. White Believes He's Ready to Play White has been on the Bills' practice squad and could get his first elevation against the Dolphins on Sunday. The veteran cornerback spoke to The Athletic and admitted he's feeling good and ready to play. "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers," the 31-year-old said. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." White, meanwhile, has also been mentoring rookie Davison Igbinosun and sophomore Maxwell Hairston. It's a different role for White, but along with mentoring, he knows he's here to play. "This ain't have to be what it was; this is what I chose," White said. "You know what I mean? I could have been anywhere else on a team, on a 53, playing right now, but I'm a Bill. … I mean, it's bigger than me, man." "I know I can go out there and play right now. Movement good, body feels good, I know how I can play, but right now my role is to help the young guys out and to be that. But it's hard, being that I just started every game last year, you know what I mean? And played good football. So it's like, ' Ahh .' But I'm going to trust the process, and I'm gonna be here to cheer the guys on. But as I'm doing it, I'm definitely preparing to play, too." The Bills are 8-1. away.headline: Dolphins get encouraging injury news on two receivers before Bills game
away.blurb: Miami’s passing game could have more help available Sunday as the Dolphins prepare for their AFC East matchup with the Buffalo Bills . Wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell are expected to play, according to NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe. Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson also reported Friday that head coach Jeff Hafley expects both receivers to be available. Douglas is dealing with a shoulder injury, while Bell has been working back from a knee injury that kept him out of Miami’s last game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the Dolphins’ official injury report, both receivers were limited participants in practice Wednesday and Thursday, His expected return would give quarterback Kyle McCord another receiving option after Miami fell 24-22 at Indianapolis on Nov. 15. Bell’s return would add another option to a group that also received contributions from Malik Washington and Jalen Tolbert. Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Tolbert on a trick play against the Colts, providing one of Miami’s biggest offensive moments. Having Douglas available and Bell back would give McCord more options as Miami tries to turn another competitive performance into a victory. The update offers good news for a receiving group that has dealt with multiple injuries throughout the week. Bell explained Thursday that he hyperextended his knee during practice last week. He did, however, express optimism about returning against Buffalo. “I think so. I hope so,” Bell said when asked whether he would play. Bell also expressed confidence that he still has more to show. “Nobody has seen the real Chris Bell yet,” he said. McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards and scored a rushing touchdown in his first NFL start. Douglas led the Dolphins with three catches for 71 yards, including a 38-yard reception that helped set up McCord’s late touchdown run. That production illustrates why Douglas’ expected availability matters. He snagged Miami’s longest reception against Indianapolis and helped create a scoring opportunity while the Dolphins were trying to erase a second-half deficit. The encouraging news does not resolve every concern at receiver, however. Jared Wayne missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with a quadriceps injury, leaving another availability question for Miami to address. The Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Soldier Field in late November isn't where a 3-6 team usually goes to turn its season around, but the New Orleans Saints are still one game behind Carolina in the NFC South. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. Facing a Dallas defense that has struggled throughout the season and already cost its coordinator his play-calling duties, Ward has a chance to deliver the best performance of his young career. As for the Cowboys, there is little evidence that a turnaround is imminent. Dallas is just 1-3 at home, has scored 123 points and allowed exactly the same number, all while its owner watches in astonishment. Titans 27, Cowboys 24 Kevin Sherrington Now that Christian Parker's no longer a target, attention turns back the head coach. Beating Tennessee offers only a temporary respite for a beleaguered staff. They're all just dead men walking. The only way they can save themselves is winning the division, then winning at least one playoff game. Nothing less will do, and even that's not enough. Cowboys 31, Titans 20 Calvin Watkins The Cowboys went through a tough week talking about the changes with Christian Parker's role. Now comes the game, and while the Titans' record shows they are terrible, there is some talent on the roster. Dallas has more talent and should have one of its easiest wins of the year. away.headline: Titans' Cam Ward gets brutal injury news as top target ruled out for season
away.blurb: In their Week 8 overtime loss against the Bengals in Cincinnati, Ward threw for a career-high 304 passing yards and two touchdowns without an interception, along with 41 rushing yards. He completed 65% of his passes and nearly won Tennessee the game. The following week, he went 28 of 39 (71.8%) for 231 yards and two touchdowns with one interception, but the Titans were blown out 40-23 by the Jaguars. They might not be in the playoff picture, but a strong finish to this season would give fans hope heading into 2027. Unfortunately for Ward, it looks like he’ll have to do it without his top target. Tennessee placed wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson on injured reserve on Tuesday with an ankle injury, and on Wednesday, Titans insider Jim Wyatt reported that Robinson is now expected to be out for the season after landing on IR. Robinson signed a four-year, $70 million contract with the Titans in March with the hope that he would help elevate Ward and give him another reliable pass catcher. Robinson had earned the contract after breaking out last season with the Giants, hauling in 92 catches on 140 targets for a career-high 1,014 yards and four touchdowns. The Tennessee Titans are just 1-8, riding a three-game losing streak, and sitting in last place in the AFC. But their offense has looked better in recent weeks, and it feels like Cam Ward may have finally found his stride. More news : CJ Stroud Makes Feelings Clear on Texans’ Season After Collapse Against Browns At 5-foot-8, 185 pounds, he’s not a traditional X receiver, but he’s valuable in the slot and behind the line of scrimmage as an athletic wideout who can make plays in space. In nine games this season, he hauled in 38 receptions on 54 targets for 272 yards and three touchdowns, leading the team in catches, targets, and touchdowns. More news : Cardinals Share Important Gardner Minshew Update After Elbow Injury More news : Chargers Face Unintended Consequence After Stunning Ravens on ‘MNF’ Losing Robinson with Ward just starting to find his groove is brutal, but the Titans do have depth at the position. First-round pick Carnell Tate should be coming back this week, while Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike have both developed a strong rapport with Ward. Veteran Calvin Ridley and tight end Gunnar Helm should help offset the loss of Robinson as well. away.headline: Tennessee Titans injury report: Carnell Tate, Anthony Hill Jr. limited
Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. home.headline: Horrific injuries revealed in Cowboys fan death as family says 49ers supporter blamed by victim
home.blurb: The 36-year-old Dallas Cowboys fan who died after an alleged altercation at AT&T Stadium claimed a 49ers fan pushed him down a flight of stairs, causing a “bulge of blood” in his stomach, according to his heartbroken family. Mario Narro traveled from Albuquerque, New Mexico, to Arlington, Texas, last weekend to watch his beloved Cowboys face the San Francisco 49ers in one of the NFL’s most storied rivalries on Sunday, Nov. 15, his niece Claudia DeLara told the California Post. Narro told a friend he attended the game with that he had gotten into a scuffle and was pushed down a flight of stairs by a Niners fan, DeLara said. “He got pushed,” DeLara exclaimed. “He fell. And immediately he had bruising and swelling in his abdomen.” Narro continued to watch the game after the fall, DeLara said, but after the final whistle on the Niners’ 46-40 victory over the Cowboys, “his friends knew that he was off.” “He wasn’t feeling like his normal self and acting like his normal self and so they made him show them his abdomen just to check to see,” DeLara told The Post. “And they said they could visibly see the bruising and, like, a bulge of blood in his abdomen,” she added. Narro’s friends rushed him to stadium medics, who transported him to a nearby hospital. He continued to insist a Niners fan had pushed him, repeating the account to doctors, DeLara said. Narro then underwent several emergency surgeries, but died from his injuries Wednesday morning. The family is still in the dark as to a specific cause of death, DeLara said. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner is conducting further testing to determine the official cause and manner of Narro’s death. “Nobody really knows what happened,” DeLara added. “We did file a police report because the only thing that we have is [Narro] said that a 49ers fan pushed him. He said that to his friend and the medical team. We don’t know what happened otherwise.” The Arlington Police Department was notified of Narro’s death on Wednesday and is currently “treating this case as a death investigation,” according to a department spokesperson. “The investigation is ongoing,” the APD added. Narro, a lifelong Cowboys fan who loved to travel and crack jokes, had visited AT&T Stadium at least two or three times before Sunday, DeLara said. “He just loved the team,” she said. Narro’s niece, Catalina Jenkins, added that she believes her uncle would still be alive “if it weren’t for this football game.” “I just want it to be clear he was an angel of a man, never hurt anyone, never had anything bad to say about anyone,” Jenkins said. “He was so loved. And I’m so sad he fell victim to such mindless violence.” California Post News: Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , X , YouTube , WhatsApp , LinkedIn California Post Sports Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , YouTube , X California Post App: Download here! home.headline: Dallas Cowboys could return veteran safety after missing seven games
home.blurb: The Cowboys carry some injuries in recent weeks to Sunday, as five players have been ruled out and four more have been ruled as questionable. Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham popped up on the injury report on Friday after not practicing with hip and groin injuries. He is listed as questionable along with tight end Luke Schoonmaker who missed Wednesday’s practice with an illness but logged full practices on Thursday and Friday. The Cowboys have two players working their way off of the injured reserve list, as rookie cornerback Devin Moore (hip) and veteran safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) each logged at least two full practices this week. For either to play, they would have to come off IR and a player already on the roster would need to be waived or put on injured reserve in their place. Thompson hasn’t played since suffering the injury in Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, while Moore hasn’t played all season. Both are officially listed as questionable. On the good news front, second-year outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku is set to return from a one-game absence after suffering an ankle injury two weeks ago. He is expected to slot back into the starting lineup with Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve. He carries no injury designation after logging a full practice on Friday and will play. Five questionable for Tennessee The Titans carry five designations into Sunday with all being listed as questionable. They join safety Tony Hill (concussion), backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and cornerback Micah Robinson (hip) as the players listed as questionable. However, all five players participated in Friday’s practice in a full capacity. After suffering high ankle sprains against the San Francisco 49ers, cornerback DaRon Bland and right guard Tyler Booker will not play against Tennessee. Each are expected to miss multiple games. Tight end Jake Ferguson will not play with knee and ankle injuries for the second week in a row after he suffered the injuries against the Indianapolis Colts. Safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) will also miss consecutive games after coming down with injuries against the Colts. Other players listed on the injury report that do not carry designations and will play include safety Malik Hooker (groin), outside linebacker James Houston (ankle), outside linebacker Von Miller (rest), defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia (finger), cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle/foot), cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (illness) and safety Juanyeh Thomas (hamstring). Standout rookies linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. (neck) and wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) are among the notables, as each have experienced strong debut campaigns in Nashville. Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. picks.blurb: Before the Roar: Previewing Lions vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Before the Roar: Previewing Lions vs. Buccaneers Morgan Cannon · SB Nation Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South hunt, and their stingy defense is one of the biggest reasons why. To break down the defense and everything else ahead of the game, Meko Scott and I are back with another episode of, " Before the Roar ." We start out with a Buccaneers' quarterback situation that seems like it's a fluid one as the week progresses. Initially, it seemed like quarterback Baker Mayfield was a bit of a longshot to play against the Lions, especially considering the moves Tampa Bay made when they signed free agent quarterback Cooper Rush, and elevated Easton Stick to the active roster from the practice squad. However, in a recent interview, Mayfield made it seem as though he would be playing if he can get cleared by Tampa Bay's medical staff. Ultimately, whoever ends up at quarterback really won't change the Lions' gameplan all that much. It all is going to hinge on Detroit's ability to stop the Buccaneers' running game. On the opposite side of the ball, the Buccaneers' defense is arguably the best in the NFL. From front-seven players like rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter and veteran nose tackle Vita Vea, to a secondary that includes the likes of Zyon McCollum and Antoine Winfield Jr, it's easy to see why this defense is so effective against just about anything that opposing offenses throw at them. Lions coach Dan Campbell and Bucs coach Todd Bowles have a long history together—dating back to when Campbell played in Dallas (2005)—and they've gone head-to-head four times in the last three seasons, with Detroit winning three of those matchups. "Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, physical unit. Known (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles a long time. Obviously have got a ton of respect for him and what he's about. And this defense is playing outstanding football. And offensively, they're committed to the run game, time of possession. They're trying to force you into making errors. And really, the last three games, they played some pretty good football." Let's take a closer look at the Bucs' coaching staff, the scheme that they run, and some scouting notes from previously viewed games. Bucs head coach: Todd Bowles NFL coaching seasons: 27 seasons (Bucs, Jets, Cardinals, Eagles, Dolphins, Cowboys, Browns) Head coaching seasons: 10 seasons (Dolphins 2011—interim, Jets 2015-18, Bucs 2022-present) Defensive coordinator seasons : 6 seasons (Eagles 2012, Cardinals 2013-14, Bucs 2019-2021) Influences: Bill Parcells, Mike Zimmer, Mike Nolan, Chuck Pagano, Paul Pasqualoni, Juan Castillo Coached under : Parcells, Bruce Arians, Andy Reid, Tony Soarano, Wade Phillips, Butch Davis, Al Groh Playcaller : Yes (Defense) Offensive coordinator: Zac Robinson NFL coaching seasons : 8 seasons (Bucs, Falcons, Rams) QB seasons in NFL : 4 years (Bengals, Lions, Seahawks, Patriots) Offensive coordinator seasons : 3 seasons (Bucs 2026, Falcons 2024-25) Previous coaching seasons : Passing game coordinator, QB coach, Assistant QB coach, Asst. WR coach Influences: Sean McVay, Bill O'Brien & Tom Brady (Pats), Kyle Shanahan Coached under : McVay, Kevin Stefanski Offensive scheme Passing game : McVay West Coast Running scheme : Shanahan outside zone and gap schemes Staples of scheme : Very similar scheme to what the Bucs have had with Baker Mayfield at QB Robinson comes from the same McVay/Shanahan tree as other former Bucs' OCs, Dave Canales (Panthers HC), Liam Coen (Jaguars HC), and Josh Grizzard (Eagles PGC) Mainly 11 Personnel: 63.3% of the time 12-personnel: 24%, 13-personnel: 8.5%, 21-personnel: 4% More shotgun (53%) than under center (37%), which is a change from previous regimes Staples: Play-action (27.5%, 8th most), pre-snap motion, and bunch formations are staples Balanced approach, pure progression reads, rhythm passing plays Want to attack and push the ball vertically QB (Mayfield, not UDFA Jalon Daniels) has the freedom at the line to check into better plays It's been an up-and-down season for Mayfield, who played in Weeks 1-3, missed Weeks 4-6 with a thumb (throwing hand) injury, returned for Weeks 7-9, and is now injured again (foot) and may not play in this game When Mayfield has played, his numbers have regressed; passer rating of 74.9 (31st in the NFL) In his six games played, he has less than 1,000 total passing yards Mayfield has more interceptions than touchdowns thrown: just 3 TDs and 4 INTs Mayfield has also fumbled six times Bottom three in the NFL in: passing yards, pass yards per play, explosive passing plays, passing success rate Offensive line has done well to mitigate pressures: 107 over nine games (8th fewest) But they've allowed 27 sacks (24th) and a 10.1% sack rate (30th) Mayfield 18 sacks over 6 games; Daniels 9 sacks over 3 games Introduced more balanced zone run concepts; a change from last year's inside zone/downhill approach Outside zone: 22.8%; inside zone: 17.2%; gap/man: 25%; Counters: 18.7% Run game has been very successful No. 1 in the NFL in average rushing yards per game: 163.9; rush yards per play: 5.0; and explosive runs over the last four games: 16.1% Success rate over last four games: 47.4% (5th) EPA per rush: -0.02 (10th) Essentially, they're wearing teams down with consistent success and hitting on big plays in the run game Dan Campbell on the Bucs' offense : "Offensively we'll see what happens with (QB) Baker (Mayfield), but obviously have got a lot of respect for him, what he's capable of, what he's done in this league. Good receivers on the perimeter. Obviously (WR Chris) Godwin (Jr.) and (WR Emeka) Egbuka over there and they got speed with (WR Tez Johnson) 15. (TE Cade) Otton's a solid tight end and this O-line is just an all-day sucker. They'll just keep coming all day long." Campbell on the Bucs' rushing attack : "Bucky (Irving)'s a hell of a back. Honestly, I should have started with him. I mean, this guy is, he really is their lifeblood for what they do offensively in this run game. And this O-line will lean on you, and they're all-day suckers, man. I mean, they will bring it all day long. And he has just got that; he's got a feel. He's got a feel for finding that crease. He understands he's got spatial awareness. He knows when these defenders are closing in on him, he can backdoor it, he can dip under, he can burst back out. And then once you get him into the second level of the defense, he's even more dangerous. So, they want to get him going here. And (RB Kenneth) Gainwell, we know too. I think Gainwell's a damn good back too. Very versatile. So, there's no secret there." Run Game Coordinator/OLB: Larry Foote For three seasons (2022-24), Foote (a Michigan native) served as the Bucs' co-defensive coordinator alongside current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers, while Bowles maintained play-calling duties. In 2025, the Bucs shifted titles, naming Foote Run Game Coordinator and outside linebackers coach. NFL coaching seasons: 12 seasons (Bucs, Cardinals) LB seasons in NFL : 13 seasons (Cardinals, Steelers, Lions) Roles with Bucs : OLB coach, Co-DC/Passing game coordinator/ILB coach, Run game coordinator/OLB coach Influences: Bruce Arians, Todd Bowles, Dick LeBeau, Jim Schwartz Coached under: Arians, Bowles, Steve Wilks Defensive scheme Base : Attacking 3-4 Coverage : Zone, single-high Staples of scheme : Aggressive, attacking scheme: 2-gapping DL and stand-up pass-rushing OLBs Nickel formations: 67% of the time means a lot of 2-4-5 formations Blitz-heavy: 43.9% (2nd most in the NFL, behind only the Vikings) Utilize blitz to rush the passer and stop the run Very creative blitzer scheme—although there's a lot of tape on Bowles' style/tendencies 3-3 Fire zones, replacement blitzing, Phantom blitzing DL stunts and slants designed to disrupt up front Pressures have declined: 112 through nine games (23rd); pressure rate: 33% (24th) As has sack production: 17 sacks (24th); sack rate: 5% (25th) Zone-heavy (85%), specifically Cover-3: 52% of the time Cover-2: 9%, Cover-4: 24%, Cover-6: 2.5% When in man coverage, it's mainly Cover-1: 9.5%, with some Cover-0 (2.5%) mixed in Bump-and-run coverage approach with corners to stay tight early in route Done well to eliminate explosive passing plays: less than 5% of attempts (No. 1 in the NFL) Done well to slow down explosive run plays: 8% (8th) Fewest rushing yards allowed per game: 79.1 (1st) Rushing yards per play: 3.5 (3rd) EPA per rush: -0.13 (3rd) Success rate over last four games: 41.2% (16th) Dan Campbell on the Bucs' defense: "They've got some impact players, guys that make it very difficult for you. Obviously (NT) Vita Vea there in the middle and (LB) Alex (Anzalone) is playing at a high level. (LB Josiah) Trotter, (S Antoine) Winfield (Jr.). I mean, we can keep going here. (DL Calijah) Kancey and they have got a ton of guys on defense playing really good football." Campbell on the Bucs' rookies making an impact: "Trotter's the best example of that. Every week he gets better and better and better in this case. The key and diagnose and his running, he's downhill and I mean he sees it and he is all out, man. I mean this guy is aggressive. So, he's really growing and he's just the best example of that, but their young guys are growing."

away.headline: Which Buccaneers stepped up as injuries piled up before the bye?
away.blurb: His involvement was growing before the comparison period ended, reaching a season-high 30 defensive snaps against Carolina in Week 7. Walker's increased playing time is particularly important with Yaya Diaby dealing with a knee injury, although the available reporting does not establish that Walker's entire increase resulted from Diaby's absence. Injuries forced Tampa Bay to adjust before the bye, but the increased playing time also created opportunities to evaluate its depth. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their Week 10 bye having dealt with injuries at quarterback, wide receiver, offensive tackle, and across the defense. Those absences forced lineup adjustments, but they also gave other players chances to show what they could contribute when called upon to step up. According to DepthRoom's snap-count data , five Buccaneers increased their share of playing time by at least 10 percentage points when comparing Weeks 4–6 with Weeks 7–9. Some stepped in for injured starters, while others saw their roles expand as personnel usage changed. Chukwuma saw the biggest increase, rising from 0% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in Weeks 4–6 to 33% over the next three games. His opportunity came when Luke Goedeke missed Week 7 against Carolina with a calf injury. Chukwuma started at right tackle and helped Tampa Bay rush for 258 yards in a 43-13 victory. According to Scott Smith's official team report , it was Chukwuma's third career start, and Todd Bowles expressed confidence in his potential to become a full-time NFL starter. Johnson's snap share climbed from 43% to 62%, with Emeka Egbuka's absence opening a spot at wide receiver. Egbuka missed Weeks 7 and 8 while dealing with concussion and foot injuries. Johnson started against Carolina and played 41 offensive snaps, contributing a 19-yard third-down reception, a 14-yard rushing gain, and a 14-yard touchdown catch. His involvement continued growing after Egbuka returned, reaching 54 snaps, or 79% of the offense, against Chicago in Week 9. Durham increased his offensive snap share from 26% to 46%, becoming a more frequent part of Tampa Bay's tight end rotation. The Buccaneers had already shown a willingness to use multiple tight ends, including opening their Week 6 matchup against Pittsburgh with three on the field. Durham's increase reflects a larger role in those personnel packages, although no specific injury has been established as the reason for his additional playing time. Perhaps the Egubka injury contributed to lineups with more tight ends on the field. Sharp's playing time rose from 6% to 23%, giving the rookie more opportunities alongside Cade Otton and Durham. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11
picks.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are 3-7 and headed to Arrowhead Stadium to face a 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs team that just beat Atlanta 35-13. They’ll do it with a 40-year-old quarterback, after Mike LaFleur said rookie Carson Beck’s back spasms have the team preparing Josh Johnson to start . Nobody expects much from Arizona in this one. Here are three bold predictions for Sunday’s noon CT kickoff. 1. Michael Wilson tops 100 receiving yards Kansas City’s defensive plan starts with Trey McBride, who has 78 catches and draws most of the short throws in this offense . That leaves Wilson as the receiver most likely to see single coverage. He has 51 catches for 546 yards, according to ESPN , second on the team behind McBride. We ran his numbers, and they show a receiver who gets volume without many big plays. Wilson has caught 51 of his 89 targets, about 57%, and he’s averaging 60.7 yards per game with a long of 27. A 100-yard day needs one or two downfield completions, and a veteran quarterback who’s been around 15 NFL rosters knows where his second option is. 2. Josh Johnson throws two touchdown passes Johnson is 2-9 in 11 career starts , and Sunday would be his first start since last season with Washington. Arizona has only 13 passing touchdowns in 10 games, and it has scored touchdowns on 42.9% of its red-zone trips. That’s why two touchdown passes is a bold call. Johnson played three games for LaFleur’s Jets in 2021, so he knows the system, and he has McBride as an easy red-zone target. If the Cardinals keep the game close into the second half, Johnson finds him twice. 3. Arizona holds Kansas City under 100 rushing yards This one goes against everything from last week. The Rams ran 46 times for 202 yards against Arizona, and the Cardinals lost two defenders to injured reserve before this trip. Arizona allows 129.9 rushing yards per game, 28th in the league. Kenneth Walker III changes the math, though. He has 872 of Kansas City’s 1,224 rushing yards, about 71%, and he missed practice again Thursday with a groin injury, according to Heavy . If Walker sits for a second straight week, the Chiefs will lean on Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce. Arizona keeps the run game in check and makes Kansas City win it through the air. The Cards are floundering, battling an inordinate number of injuries at the skill positions, and now starting rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has the Chiefs in first in the AFC West and just one game behind Buffalo for the top spot in the AFC (Spoiler Alert: the Bills and Chiefs play on Thanksgiving on NBC/Peacock .) It should come as no surprise that the statistical gap is significant: the Cardinals average just 18.4 points per game while allowing 28.9, whereas Kansas City scores 26.3 per game and owns one of the league’s stingiest defenses at 17.3 points allowed per game…and KC is undefeated at home this season (4-0). The Cardinals are coming off an ugly 34-6 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game in which their offense essentially disappeared after the opening quarter. Two 49-yard field goals from Chad Ryland gave Arizona a 6-3 lead, but those would be its only points. Beck, making his first NFL start, completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions, while the Cardinals managed only 142 total yards, 34 rushing yards and six first downs. They went 0-for-6 on third down and held the ball for just 17:37. Trey McBride led the team with five catches for 37 yards. The Chiefs delivered a performance that was basically the exact opposite of that put forth by the Cards. KC rolled past the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 for their second straight win. Mahomes was sensational, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns without throwing an interception. Rookie Emmett Johnson carried the ball 22 times for 101 yards and also caught a touchdown pass, helping Kansas City pile up 461 yards of total offense. The Kansas City defense forced two turnovers and held Atlanta to one touchdown in five red-zone trips. These teams do not meet often, but the recent regular-season history decidedly favors Kansas City. The Chiefs have won the last two meetings, including a 44-21 victory at Arizona in the 2022 season opener, when Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, and a 26-14 win at Arrowhead Stadium in 2018; the Cardinals’ last regular-season victory in the series was 17-14 in 2014.
