picks.headline: Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. Kansas City enters 7-2, while Arizona has lost two straight to fall to 3-7. The betting line lists the Chiefs as 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals. The prediction picks Kansas City to beat Arizona 33-9 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here’s what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday’s monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year’s Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. “He’s obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college,” Tranquill said of Beck. “He’ll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it’s a good opportunity for him, but we’ll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground.” With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals’ best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona’s struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that’s left McBride as Beck’s lone viable option. Among Arizona’s available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. “They’ve got some good tight ends, and so we’ll have to be on it,” Tranquill said. “They’re big, they’re physical, can make contested catches. And so we’ll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys.” Arizona’s protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals’ offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn’t get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn’t practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals’ secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it’s that they’re more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. “They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses,” Mahomes said. “There’s been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It’s not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don’t, they’ll get home, and they’ll cause negative plays.” Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City’s practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Rashee Rice led the Chiefs with 82 yards, and Downs, Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen all reached the end zone. Sunday’s game will give way to a short Thanksgiving week for the Chiefs, with perhaps their most important game of the season awaiting them Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Given the grand disparity between the two clubs, look for head coach Andy Reid to be mindful about how long he plays some of his key contributors, especially those dealing with injuries. Cardinals-Chiefs game prediction In my 13 years analyzing and previewing Chiefs games, I’m not sure that I can recall a matchup this lopsided going in. But as they say, that’s why they play the games. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. They had won four straight before being embarrassed on national television by the Bengals, 38-18. The Eagles are no strangers to embarrassment this season, but for the first time in several weeks, the injury report isn't looking like a CVS receipt. WR DeVonta Smith practiced in full Thursday, as did RB Saquon Barkley, and edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt. HC Mike McCarthy is in his first season coaching Pittsburgh, but has plenty of experience coaching against the Eagles from his days in Green Bay and Dallas. He is 3-5 lifetime in games at the Linc. Nick Sirianni is 5-0 after a bye week, but I'm not sure any amount of time will give his team enough of an advantage. Picks: Steelers -4.5 Passing Props (O/U) Aaron Rodgers: 211.5 passing yards, 1.5 TD (+140/-188) Joe Milton: 187.5 passing yards, 0.5 TD (-205/+152) Analysis: Milton did his best with the hand he was dealt two weeks ago against the Giants (18/34/169), considering he spent much of the afternoon running for his life. He'll get help with Smith – and very possibly Tay Wicks – returning to the lineup. He should also get a boost from a Steelers pass D ranked 30 th in the league. Rodgers has had an up-and-down season; he had a four-week run where he looked bulletproof, and followed it up with two games with subpar numbers: a blowout win over Cleveland, where they didn't need much from him, and their blowout loss to the Bengals, where they didn't get much. Picks: Milton OVER yards, Rodgers OVER yards Rushing Props (O/U) Jaylen Warren – 65.5 yards Saquon Barkley – 60.5 yards Rico Dowdle – 37.5 yards Milton – 34.5 yards Analysis: I feel a lot of the game script could be determined by which Jaylen Warren shows up. He has had five games with 93+ yards this season, and four with 50 or fewer, the most recent last week vs Cincy (7/15). Dowdle had three straight games of 40+ yards before last week's 5/26. I like Milton to make more plays with his legs, as he did vs NYG (9/64). It may be a better strategy than running Barkley between the tackles. Barkley may finally be healthy, but he can't block for himself. Picks: Barkley UNDER yards, Milton OVER yards Receiving Props (O/U) DeVonta Smith – 48.5 yards, 4.5 receptions DK Metcalf – 42.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Dallas Goedert – 30.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Germie Bernard – 29.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Warren – 22.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Pat Freiermuth – 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Darnell Washington 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Barkley – 10.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Dowdle – 9.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Analysis: One would think Smith will want to put on a show after missing 5 of the last 6 games, and a change in QB from Tanner McKee to Milton shouldn't put a wrinkle in that. Goedert has caught 4+ passes in L5. I can't explain what happened to DK Metcalf. 35 catches in nine games is far less than I expected, and I think Steelers fans would agree. Five catches on 28 targets over the last 3 weeks is shocking. Meanwhile, Bernard had a four-game run of 25 catches before being shutout last week. Warren has 3 catches in 6/9 this season, and 26+ yards in 8/9, he's Rodgers' main checkdown option. Picks: Smith OVER yards, OVER receptions; Warren OVER receptions, OVER yards Anytime Touchdown Washington +300 Freiermuth +330 Analysis: Either Steelers TE has scored in six straight. Play them both, just not in a parlay. Picks: Barkley, Milton, Washington, Freiermuth

Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles will face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday without linebacker Zack Baun and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks. The Eagles ruled both out Friday and listed linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. as doubtful, leaving Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. in line to start inside. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is set to return after practicing in full for a second straight day. Campbell is set to return with Baun out Campbell and Trotter will have to account for Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren, who has 719 rushing yards and 320 receiving yards. The Steelers can use him underneath when Aaron Rodgers gets the ball out quickly, putting Philadelphia’s linebackers in position to make tackles in space. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard did not practice Friday and was listed with an ankle injury and rest. He received no game designation. Nolan Smith, who had been limited with an illness, was upgraded to full participation Friday and also has no designation. DeVonta Smith is available for Joe Milton’s second start Smith has missed five of the past six games with a hamstring injury. He was listed as limited Wednesday before practicing in full Thursday and Friday. Wicks was limited Friday with ankle and foot injuries and will miss his fourth straight game. Both sat out against the Giants, when rookie Makai Lemon led Philadelphia with six catches for 61 yards in Milton’s first Eagles start. Running back Will Shipley was listed as questionable with a foot injury and an illness after missing Friday’s practice. He is in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. Returner Britain Covey was limited with a knee injury and received no game designation. Defensive backs Michael Carter II and Jonathan Jones were upgraded to full participation. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles rule out Zack Baun and Dontayvion Wicks for game vs. Steelers Baun missed all three practices this week after injuring his back against the New York Giants before the bye. Mondon replaced him alongside Trotter in that game, but he missed Thursday and Friday with an ankle injury. Campbell practiced in full all week after missing the past two games with hamstring and quadriceps injuries.

away.headline: Steelers' injury report highlighted by Nick Herbig's status vs. Eagles
away.blurb: Most of those questions are positive ones for the Steelers - like will wide receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. both return against the Eagles or just one? Will they activate rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker from the IR? But as the positive news mounts, the Steelers are never too far from a setback. With the team's latest injury report ahead of their Week 11 matchup, another player is now the biggest concern. Outside linebacker Nick Herbig did not participate in two previous practices due to a rib and hip injury, and after being designated as not participating in a third straight team session, he has been listed as questionable against the Eagles. Additionally, the Steelers listed Dunker, Pittman, Wilson, inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and safety DeShon Elliott as questionable. Queen is dealing with a fractured thumb he sustained in Week 10, but is expected to play, while Elliott missed Week 10 due to a knee injury he suffered pregame. As far as the other players on the report, part of that feels far easier to decipher. Both Pittman Jr. and Wilson have been full participants in practice this week. That's the strongest indication that both could return to the lineup. Add in the fact that the Steelers waived receiver Brandon Smith, and it feels like a foregone conclusion that both pass-catchers are in the lineup against the Eagles. Dunker is not so clear-cut, in my opinion. The Steelers need the third-round pick to be able to suit up, simply due to the lack of available offensive lineman. After Mason McCormick was placed on Injured Reserve due to a dislocated ankle, the Steelers have just seven healthy offensive linemen on the active roster. He finished Week 10 playing 28 defensive and 12 special teams snaps. It was just a slight decrease in share of the snap count compared to previous weeks. More concerning is how much this will hamper Herbig moving forward. It's already been a difficult 2026 campaign for the fourth-year EDGE rusher. He is fourth on the team in sacks, with 3.0 in nine games, but he's currently being outproduced by T.J. Watt (7.5 sacks) and Alex Highsmith (3.5 sacks), as well as inside linebacker Patrick Queen (3.5 sacks). Even if Herbig plays in Week 11, there's no telling how close to 100% healthy he truly is. They extended it with a 27-13 win in 2024, holding Pittsburgh scoreless after halftime and running out the final 10:29. With the team's latest injury report ahead of their Week 11 matchup, another player is now the biggest concern. Outside linebacker Nick Herbig did not participate in two previous practices due to a rib and hip injury, and after being designated as not participating in a third straight team session, he has been listed as questionable against the Eagles. Additionally, the Steelers listed Dunker, Pittman, Wilson, inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and safety DeShon Elliott as questionable. Queen is dealing with a fractured thumb he sustained in Week 10, but is expected to play, while Elliott missed Week 10 due to a knee injury he suffered pregame. As far as the other players on the report, part of that feels far easier to decipher. Both Pittman Jr. and Wilson have been full participants in practice this week. That's the strongest indication that both could return to the lineup. Add in the fact that the Steelers waived receiver Brandon Smith, and it feels like a foregone conclusion that both pass-catchers are in the lineup against the Eagles. Dunker is not so clear-cut, in my opinion. The Steelers need the third-round pick to be able to suit up, simply due to the lack of available offensive lineman. After Mason McCormick was placed on Injured Reserve due to a dislocated ankle, the Steelers have just seven healthy offensive linemen on the active roster. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. home.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. Panthers get Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble back on the field This article originally appeared on Ravens Wire: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game

The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! New York has lost five contests in a row, the last two of which were blowout defeats at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills. While the Chargers are technically headed in the other direction after securing their first win of the year, Los Angeles still looks like one of the worst teams in football on a week-to-week basis. Getting a second consecutive win would be a good start in changing that perception. While New York is coming off a couple of blowout losses, those defeats did come against a few of the best teams in football. When head coach Aaron Glenn's squad faced teams like the New England Patriots, Miami Dolphins, and Las Vegas Raiders, the Jets hung tough, losing each game on the outcome of one or two plays. If those performances are any indication, New York should be plenty capable of keeping things close with the Chargers. Quarterback Geno Smith will have to play a turnover-free game, while the defense, led by rookie defensive end David Bailey, plays mistake-free football. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel finally seemed to get things to click in the Chargers' last game against the Baltimore Ravens. Giving running back Omarion Hampton an extended run for the first time in ages helped revive a ground attack that seemed dead in the water only a couple of weeks ago. If McDaniel knows what's good for his job security, he will give Hampton the touches he earned last week. Unfortunately, the offensive line did not fare as well in pass protection as it did in the run game, leaving quarterback Justin Herbert out to dry far too often. A fearsome New York defensive line will present an even bigger challenge than Baltimore did, making it difficult for the Chargers to win their second game of the year. (AP) — New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was a full participant at practice Friday and removed from the injury report, putting him on track to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. “He'll be practicing fully today, so we'll see how that goes,” coach Aaron Glenn said before practice Friday. “He looks solid. It's very encouraging.” The Jets (2-8) are looking to snap a five-game losing streak when they face the Chargers (1-8), who got their first win when they beat Baltimore on Monday night. Smith was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik last week. Tight ends Mason Taylor and rookie Kenyon Sadiq could also see increased targets in the passing game. “I think that's the good thing about the tight end room is those guys can actually end up playing some of those receiver spots that we have,” Glenn said. Williams is the Jets' primary punt returner, so Isaiah Davis could assume that role. Williams also shares kickoff duties with Kene Nwangwu. Defensive lineman David Onyemata, on injured reserve the past eight weeks with an abdominal injury, won't be activated from injured reserve this week, Glenn said. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Denver Broncos vs. Las Vegas Raiders in week 11
picks.blurb: The Denver Broncos come out of their bye at 7-2 with a five-game winning streak, and Jonah Coleman gets a Las Vegas Raiders run defense that has been one of the worst in football. Sunday’s game at Empower Field kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, and it’s the first look at whether Sean Payton fixed anything during the week off . Here are three bold predictions for how Denver handles the 4-6 Raiders. Jonah Coleman runs for 100 yards Coleman has taken the lead back job from J.K. Dobbins , and the numbers explain why. He’s averaging 4.1 yards per carry with three touchdowns on 47 carries, while Dobbins is at 3.3 on 98 carries. His best game so far is 57 yards at Carolina. Line those up against what Las Vegas allows and the opening is obvious. The Raiders give up 151.1 rushing yards per game, 31st in the NFL, according to the Raiders’ game preview . Denver’s offense averages just 91.4 on the ground. The Raiders’ interior is also banged up, with defensive tackles Tonka Hemingway and Foley Fatukasi missing Thursday’s practice, per the Broncos’ injury report . Coleman gets his first 100-yard game. Zach Allen sacks Fernando Mendoza twice Allen made PFF’s midseason All-Pro team , and he has 4.5 sacks from the interior. Nik Bonitto also has 4.5, and Denver’s 26 sacks rank in the top 10. Mendoza was sacked six times by Seattle in his first start, and this is his first road start. The rookie had a strong first half against the Seahawks before the protection broke down, and Denver’s pass rush should feast on a quarterback still learning to read pressure. Allen gets two of the Broncos’ four sacks. Pat Surtain II gets his first interception of the season This one is bold because Surtain doesn’t have an interception yet. He missed three games, and teams have mostly stayed away from him. Receivers are averaging under nine yards per catch against him, according to the Raiders’ preview. Tre Tucker is the Raiders’ top outside threat with 538 yards on 15.8 yards per catch, and Surtain should see plenty of him. With Riley Moss newly extended on the other side , Mendoza won’t find many easy throws to the perimeter. Brock Bowers was limited Thursday with ankle and quadriceps injuries, and he leads the Raiders with 50 catches. If Bowers is limited Sunday, Mendoza has to look outside more often, and that’s where Surtain lives. He picks off the rookie, and Denver wins 24-13 for its sixth straight. away.headline: Brock Bowers returns to practice ahead of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 matchup against Denver Broncos
away.blurb: The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues.

away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Raiders Reveal Brock Bowers’ Injury Status vs. Broncos
away.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders appear to have avoided disaster with tight end Brock Bowers. He rolled his ankle against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10, which forced him to sit out the second half. However, the Raiders aren’t ready to commit to him playing against the Denver Broncos in Week 11. Head coach Klint Kubiak announced that Bowers will be listed as questionable vs. the Broncos. That means he’ll likely travel with the team and test out his ankle to see if he can play. That’s a promising step for the Raiders. The offense has a very hard time moving the ball when he isn’t on the field. He then missed Wednesday’s practice, which is never a good sign. Luckily, he returned to practice on Thursday and Friday. That means it’s nothing long-term. The Broncos have another very good defense, so they need Bowers if they’re hoping to score points. The young tight end has proven to be a very tough player, so if it’s up to him, he’ll likely try to play. The Raiders may have to save him from himself, but they also need a win against Denver. This will continue to be a situation to watch closely ahead of the game. Kubiak grew up around the Broncos. His father played for and coached the team. Kubiak’s first NFL job was coaching for the Broncos. Since he’s been around the franchise for much of his life, it would make sense if he had a previous bias against the Raiders. Instead, he used to be worried about whether the Broncos would play them. “I was always nervous,” Kubiak said, via The Athletic . “Like, they’re playing Rich Gannon and Jerry Rice this week, man. I hope they win.” Raiders Hall of Fame wide receiver Tim Brown also played a big influence on Kubiak. “Just as a young kid, getting to watch on the sideline, those are your heroes,” Kubiak said. “I just kind of remember the snow falling down in the stadium and watching those guys run on the field. And Tim Brown’s got his finger tape rolled up, and then that week in my game, I’m rolling up my fingers. Tim Brown doesn’t need gloves, neither do I.” Kubiak Discusses How He Got Raiders Job The Raiders franchise hates the Broncos, so Kubiak had that working against him when he interviewed for the job. Luckily, the interview process went really well for both sides. “I just figured, ‘Hey, I’m gonna go be myself and tell them what I know, and if that’s good enough, that’s OK,’” Kubiak said. “As the interview unfolded, it just started gnawing at me, like, these are people that I want to work with. This would be an extremely special opportunity. And I just remember that at some point in the interview, I could just kind of feel my heart like getting really excited for what could be here with the Raiders, and wanted to be a part of it.” Kubiak is a Raider now, so he’s going to quickly learn to hate the Broncos franchise despite how much they’ve given his family. away.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
away.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. Now, they're up against it. Broncos' injury report is as thin as it gets before clash with Raiders Both teams released their injury reports after Wednesday's practice. Here is how things went in Denver: Nobody is wishing injury on the Broncos, but of course, as fate would have it, they get a handful of key players back when they face the Raiders. Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss, both of whom suffered concussions in Week 9, are back at practice with no limitations and will play on Sunday. Talanoa Hufanga is also back this week, it seems, after missing four straight games for the Broncos' secondary. He was playing well before suffering an ankle injury, and he missed an entire month. But with an extra week off to prepare, he will re-emerge against the Raiders, of course. Caleb Loehner is also back this week after beginning the season on IR. He is a promising young tight end prospect that, if you can believe anything that Sean Payton says, has a bright future in Denver. away.headline: Raiders star tight end appears to have avoided a more serious injury, report says
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is “day to day” with the ankle injury that knocked him out Sunday’s 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, coach Klint Kubiak said Monday afternoon. Running back Ashton Jeanty rolled up on Bowers’ leg during a first-quarter run. Bowers went into the injury tent, returned to play and they left through the tunnel during quaterback Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start. He’s leading the Raiders with 50 receptions, 676 receiving yards and six touchdowns receptions. He departed play Sunday with two receptions for 18 yards, having eclipsed 70-plus receiving yards in his first seven games. “It’s not as bad as we thought,” Kubiak said, “but it still is a significant injury, so we’ll keep monitoring him.” The Raiders struggled to make a first down in the second half, going 0 of 7 on third-down conversions. “When you lose one of your best players, I think that affects things,” Kubiak said. “But we’ve got lots of playmakers on the field. There’s more production to be had than what we did in that second half.” Las Vegas travels to play Sunday against the Denver Broncos. Contact Sam Gordon at sgordon@reviewjournal.com. home.headline: Brock Bowers returns to practice ahead of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 matchup against Denver Broncos
home.blurb: The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues.

home.headline: Raiders Reveal Brock Bowers’ Injury Status vs. Broncos
home.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders appear to have avoided disaster with tight end Brock Bowers. He rolled his ankle against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10, which forced him to sit out the second half. However, the Raiders aren’t ready to commit to him playing against the Denver Broncos in Week 11. Head coach Klint Kubiak announced that Bowers will be listed as questionable vs. the Broncos. That means he’ll likely travel with the team and test out his ankle to see if he can play. That’s a promising step for the Raiders. The offense has a very hard time moving the ball when he isn’t on the field. He then missed Wednesday’s practice, which is never a good sign. Luckily, he returned to practice on Thursday and Friday. That means it’s nothing long-term. The Broncos have another very good defense, so they need Bowers if they’re hoping to score points. The young tight end has proven to be a very tough player, so if it’s up to him, he’ll likely try to play. The Raiders may have to save him from himself, but they also need a win against Denver. This will continue to be a situation to watch closely ahead of the game. Kubiak grew up around the Broncos. His father played for and coached the team. Kubiak’s first NFL job was coaching for the Broncos. Since he’s been around the franchise for much of his life, it would make sense if he had a previous bias against the Raiders. Instead, he used to be worried about whether the Broncos would play them. “I was always nervous,” Kubiak said, via The Athletic . “Like, they’re playing Rich Gannon and Jerry Rice this week, man. I hope they win.” Raiders Hall of Fame wide receiver Tim Brown also played a big influence on Kubiak. “Just as a young kid, getting to watch on the sideline, those are your heroes,” Kubiak said. “I just kind of remember the snow falling down in the stadium and watching those guys run on the field. And Tim Brown’s got his finger tape rolled up, and then that week in my game, I’m rolling up my fingers. Tim Brown doesn’t need gloves, neither do I.” Kubiak Discusses How He Got Raiders Job The Raiders franchise hates the Broncos, so Kubiak had that working against him when he interviewed for the job. Luckily, the interview process went really well for both sides. “I just figured, ‘Hey, I’m gonna go be myself and tell them what I know, and if that’s good enough, that’s OK,’” Kubiak said. “As the interview unfolded, it just started gnawing at me, like, these are people that I want to work with. This would be an extremely special opportunity. And I just remember that at some point in the interview, I could just kind of feel my heart like getting really excited for what could be here with the Raiders, and wanted to be a part of it.” Kubiak is a Raider now, so he’s going to quickly learn to hate the Broncos franchise despite how much they’ve given his family. home.headline: Will Brock Bowers play for the Raiders against the Broncos? What we know about the TE’s injury
home.blurb: The Raiders tight end returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday with ankle and quadriceps injuries. Bowers has been dealing with ankle and quadriceps injuries after leaving last Sunday’s 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His availability remains uncertain, but his return to the practice field is a positive development for the Raiders as they prepare for a difficult divisional matchup. As of Friday morning, November 20, Bowers has not been officially ruled in or out for Sunday’s game. However, his return to practice on Thursday has improved the outlook for his availability. The tight end was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout. The Raiders listed both an ankle and a quadriceps injury on their report. Kubiak also indicated that Bowers might not need to practice this week to be available against Denver. His participation on Thursday nevertheless represents an important step toward a possible return. The Raiders are scheduled to practice again Friday , when another update on Bowers’ condition is expected. The team’s final injury report should provide a clearer indication of whether he will be available against the Broncos. He caught a pass after coming back onto the field, but the ankle continued to bother him and he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Bowers finished with two receptions for 18 yards, a significant loss for the offense, who rely heavily on his ability to create opportunities in the passing game. His potential return would be significant for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is preparing for just his second NFL start . Bowers gives the young quarterback one of his most reliable targets against a Denver defense that has been among the league’s strongest this season. If Bowers is unavailable, Michael Mayer would be expected to take on a larger role in the Raiders’ offense. Mendoza has also highlighted the other options available to him, including wide receivers Jack Bech and Tre Tucker , as well as tight end Ian Thomas. The Raiders will hope Bowers can make enough progress to return against Denver, but his status will depend on how he responds to the remainder of the week’s practices. For now, Thursday’s limited participation is an encouraging sign . The Raiders are still waiting for confirmation that their star tight end will be ready to play on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.
