But as the Giants prepare for the upcoming game, this could be a real challenge for the team to deal with. New York will be hosting the Jacksonville Jaguars this week, giving the team a true test to overcome. For the year, the Giants hold a record of 5-3-1, sitting in first place of the NFC East, at least for now. New York has been trying to get back to the playoffs, and this game against Jacksonville could help out greatly. As for the Jaguars, they will enter the game with a record of 7-2 for the season, sitting in first place of the AFC South. Jacksonville is among the top teams in the NFL, and they may be the most well-rounded roster in the league. But the Giants will try to pull off the upset at home, and New York has been very good playing at MetLife this year. New York is 3-2 at home this season, giving them a slight edge entering the contest with Jacksonville. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report made game picks for all matchups in Week 11. Within these, only two of the seven picked the Giants to grab the victory at home over the Jaguars. Only Gagnon and Hanford went with the Giants to get the win, which speaks to the level of trust in the team. But Jacksonville is one of the stronger teams in the NFL, and this could be a tough matchup for New York. The big key in this game will be the play from quarterback J.J. McCarthy against a tough Jaguars defense. McCarthy will look to bounce back from a costly turnover in the team's last game, but that could be easier said than done. So far this season, McCarthy has thrown for 915 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. The former first-round draft pick has helped spark new life into the Giants' offense, but the team needs more from him going forward. For New York to take down the Jaguars, McCarthy will need to push the ball down the field, keeping up with the scoring. Jacksonville has been a lethal offense, and the Giants can't afford to settle for field goals or turnovers.

picks.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing the Jaguars' Matchup With Giants, J.J. McCarthy, and More
picks.blurb: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing the Jaguars' Matchup With Giants, J.J. McCarthy, and More - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) motions during a game against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium, Nov 12, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect John Shipley · Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:31 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Jacksonville Jaguars, this is a big one. The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks. To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect. So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below. 1) What is Arvell Reese more dangerous at: playing linebacker or rushing the passer? Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started. Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role. 2) How do you view the matchup between Malik Nabers and Travis Hunter? Traina: I think that's going to be a key matchup. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has done a good job of scheming Nabers open this season by moving him around the formation. When playing in the slot, he has an 84.6% reception rate and has scored both of his touchdowns from the slot. Travis Hunter hasn't worked much from the slot this season. They have Hunter down as having played six total snaps in the slot, defending just one target that was not completed. I am very interested in seeing how much the Giants put Nabers in the slot on Sunday and, when he's not in the slot, how much, if any, the Jaguars have Hunter travel with him. 3) How much have the Giants trusted J.J. McCarthy when it comes to attacking defenses downfield? Explosive plays have been one of the Jaguars' few weaknesses. Traina: Overall, the Giants have a 44.7% passing completion rate (10th in the league) on deep balls of 20+ air yards. This season, McCarthy has a 52.6% completion rate on deep passes of 20+ air yards. As you might guess, Nabers has been the main target on those deep balls., he's caught 12 of 21 (57.1%) with one drop. Rookie Malachi Fields has caught three of nine, and Darnell Mooney one of six. Tight end Isaiah Likely has caught three of seven deep passes. As I'm guessing the Jaguars will do everything possible to take Nabers out of the equation, I suspect this could be a good opportunity for Fields to have a breakout game. 4) What kind of impact has former Jaguars CB Greg Newsome made in New York? Traina: He's been outstanding in coverage, so much so that the Giants recently gave him a three-year contract extension. He currently has a career-best 71.2 coverage grade from PFF and has allowed opponents just a 57.6% completion rate. Newsome has also allowed just 61 YAC, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has five pass breakups, all good for a 63.8 NFL coverage rating, which is the best of his career. 5) If Jacksonville wins this game, what do you think would be the biggest reason why? They make the Giants one-dimensional. The Jaguars have one of the best run defenses in the league right now, and I'm fairly certain they'll zero in on shutting down running back Cam Skattebo and challenging McCarthy to beat them through the air. McCarthy is 9-4 as a starter in games where his offense has rushed for 100+ yards collectively. That's not to say McCarthy and the Giants can't pull off the upset, but if they become one-dimensional, it'll be that much harder for them to do so. As my readers and listeners have reminded me, the Giants ran up a storm against the Houston Texans a few weeks back, posting a season-high 188 yards against a Texans run defense that was top five going into that game. So yes, the Giants have a chance. home.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
home.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. picks.blurb: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has transformed the NFC playoff picture since being traded from Las Vegas to Minnesota at the trade deadline, and that’s set up a very interesting Sunday Night Football matchup in Week 11. The Vikings are set to face the San Francisco 49ers in a neutral site game in Mexico City, and there are a ton of playoff implications at stake. Not only are the Vikings battling for first place in the NFC North, but a win over San Fran would give Minnesota a legit shot at the No. 1 seed in the conference. A Cousins trade materialized for Minnesota after back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo where Kyler Murray (against Detroit) and Carson Wentz (against Buffalo) showed that they simply aren’t playing quarterback at a high enough level for the Vikings to win a Super Bowl. That sentiment has changed in the futures market, as the Vikings are now priced around 15/1 to win it all after an upset win over Green Bay in Week 10. The odds for that game shifted in a big way after Cousins was acquired, as the same goes for Week 11 against San Francisco. Sports Illustrated spoke to several oddsmakers this week to see just how much the Cousins’ acquisition has changed the Vikings’ outlook in this Sunday Night matchup. How Much Kirk Cousins Impacts Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for NFL Week 11 The Vikings opened as 3.5-point underdogs in Week 11 after their win over Green Bay, but that line has continued to move towards the Vikings, settling at 3. While that’s a minor move, there’s a chance this line would have been set as far as 49ers -7 if Murray or Wentz was under center on Sunday night. “Well, if the quarterback play continued to go the way it was before Cousins arrived, the Vikings would have been close to a touchdown underdog, rather than a field goal underdog,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. That’s at least a four-point swing in favor of the 49ers, though not every book had that price. BetMGM and FanDuel both told Sports Illustrated that the spread would likely be close to four or five. “Not too much believe it or not, probably was about a point or so move,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. The reason being is there isn't a major gap between Cousins and Murray. The main reason for this spread being close is the strength of the defense. Both QBs are capable, it helps Minnesota's future odds more because if one gets injured they have a capable backup to come in.” It’s interesting to hear about different pricing across the industry, as Fanatics has a much different grade – but similar to DraftKings – when it comes to the Murray vs. Cousins debate: “We opened up a lookahead line on the day of trade deadline day, it was plus seven,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “And now the Vikings are three-point dogs, just to give you an idea of how highly we rate Kirk Cousins versus Murray or Wentz.” In his first start with the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two scores and one pick, and he has 22 touchdown passes in the 2026 season. There’s no doubt that this Vikings team – which has the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play in 2026 – has a much better chance of competing with San Fran’s No. 1 offense with Cousins calling the shots. What Would the Vikings vs. 49ers Spread Be in San Francisco? This game is also unusual because of the neutral site aspect. While this is technically a home game for San Francisco, it likely would be favored by more Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. Still, Avello explained that home field doesn’t matter as much as it used to when DraftKings sets the spread for games. “ The Niners playing at home – there's a misconception with home-field advantage,” Avello said. When you look at it across the league, it's only a couple of points. Some teams get a little stronger, and a lot of it has to do with weather. So, the Niners would have been only maybe another point and a half at home, so maybe the line would have been 4.5.” San Francisco is a perfect 5-0 at home in the 2026 season, so it’ll be interesting to see if Kyle Shanahan’s team can hold up on a neutral field. The 49ers (8-1) are looking to maintain their lead in the NFC and NFC West, but a loss to Minnesota would bring it back down into the same playing field with other two-loss teams like Chicago and Detroit. picks.headline: 3 bold Vikings predictions before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City
picks.blurb: Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. away.headline: 49ers' Mike Evans on track to play vs. Vikings after missing past month with Achilles injury
away.blurb: Matt Barrows Share Facebook Share Twitter AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. -- Mike Evans practiced Thursday and Friday, putting the veteran receiver in position to return Sunday in Mexico City against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that he would check in with Evans on Saturday to see how the two days of practice affected the Achilles tendonitis that kept him sidelined for more than a month. Evans was limited in both practices and is listed as questionable on the team's injury report. "Having Mike out there -- everyone knows how good Mike is," Shanahan said. "I think the guys have done a good job holding it down with him not out there, but Mike's our guy and a very unique player, and he's been doing it at a high level for a very long time. Played really unbelievable for the games he played in this year, and it'd be great to get him back." Though some players like Evans are questionable for the game, all 53 players on the 49ers' active roster took part in Friday's practice, a rarity for the injury-addled team. He went into the Week 6 game against the Washington Commanders with Achilles tendinitis, which caused him to come out of the contest. He hasn't played or practiced since. If Evans, 33, plays, he'd join Deebo Samuel, 30, Demarcus Robinson 32, Brandin Cooks, 33 and Keenan Allen, 34, as thirty-something receivers available against the Vikings. Over the past 18 years, the league's domestic fan base has surged from roughly 10 million to 40 million, according to the NFL. "We have grown significantly over these years thanks to the constant, continuous, daily work of our team," Olivé said. "Eighteen years ago, we chose our battles and focused our attention on the specific areas we needed to improve in order to expand our fan base." In Mexico, the NFL trails only soccer — the national sport — in total fans. The game's popularity is no coincidence; American football is as much a part of Mexican sports tradition as soccer, boxing, and lucha libre. The Mexico game will be the last of the nine international NFL games played this season, a league record. To expand its reach, NFL Mexico invested heavily in flag football, which has steadily gained traction and now boasts roughly 4 million players nationwide. While impressive, Olivé acknowledges that in a nation of more than 130 million people, there is still vast room for growth. To accelerate adoption, the league signed an agreement with the National Commission of Physical Culture and Sport (CONADE) to expand the sport across public schools. "With 4 million children in the program, we are barely scratching the surface. Forty million fans in Mexico is a lot, but there are still another 80 or 90 million people we could reach," Olivé said. CONADE, the agency that oversees Mexico's federal sports budget, is eager to promote flag football ahead of its debut as an Olympic sport at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. "We believe this alliance turns schools into spaces for participation, well-being and talent development," said Rommel Pacheco, general director of CONADE. home.headline: 49ers' Mike Evans on track to play vs. Vikings after missing past month with Achilles injury
home.blurb: Matt Barrows Share Facebook Share Twitter AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. -- Mike Evans practiced Thursday and Friday, putting the veteran receiver in position to return Sunday in Mexico City against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that he would check in with Evans on Saturday to see how the two days of practice affected the Achilles tendonitis that kept him sidelined for more than a month. Evans was limited in both practices and is listed as questionable on the team's injury report. "Having Mike out there -- everyone knows how good Mike is," Shanahan said. "I think the guys have done a good job holding it down with him not out there, but Mike's our guy and a very unique player, and he's been doing it at a high level for a very long time. Played really unbelievable for the games he played in this year, and it'd be great to get him back." Though some players like Evans are questionable for the game, all 53 players on the 49ers' active roster took part in Friday's practice, a rarity for the injury-addled team. He went into the Week 6 game against the Washington Commanders with Achilles tendinitis, which caused him to come out of the contest. He hasn't played or practiced since. If Evans, 33, plays, he'd join Deebo Samuel, 30, Demarcus Robinson 32, Brandin Cooks, 33 and Keenan Allen, 34, as thirty-something receivers available against the Vikings. home.headline: Horrific injuries revealed in Cowboys fan death as family says 49ers supporter blamed by victim
home.blurb: The 36-year-old Dallas Cowboys fan who died after an alleged altercation at AT&T Stadium claimed a 49ers fan pushed him down a flight of stairs, causing a “bulge of blood” in his stomach, according to his heartbroken family. Mario Narro traveled from Albuquerque, New Mexico, to Arlington, Texas, last weekend to watch his beloved Cowboys face the San Francisco 49ers in one of the NFL’s most storied rivalries on Sunday, Nov. 15, his niece Claudia DeLara told the California Post. Narro told a friend he attended the game with that he had gotten into a scuffle and was pushed down a flight of stairs by a Niners fan, DeLara said. “He got pushed,” DeLara exclaimed. “He fell. And immediately he had bruising and swelling in his abdomen.” Narro continued to watch the game after the fall, DeLara said, but after the final whistle on the Niners’ 46-40 victory over the Cowboys, “his friends knew that he was off.” “He wasn’t feeling like his normal self and acting like his normal self and so they made him show them his abdomen just to check to see,” DeLara told The Post. “And they said they could visibly see the bruising and, like, a bulge of blood in his abdomen,” she added. Narro’s friends rushed him to stadium medics, who transported him to a nearby hospital. He continued to insist a Niners fan had pushed him, repeating the account to doctors, DeLara said. Narro then underwent several emergency surgeries, but died from his injuries Wednesday morning. The family is still in the dark as to a specific cause of death, DeLara said. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner is conducting further testing to determine the official cause and manner of Narro’s death. “Nobody really knows what happened,” DeLara added. “We did file a police report because the only thing that we have is [Narro] said that a 49ers fan pushed him. He said that to his friend and the medical team. We don’t know what happened otherwise.” The Arlington Police Department was notified of Narro’s death on Wednesday and is currently “treating this case as a death investigation,” according to a department spokesperson. “The investigation is ongoing,” the APD added. Narro, a lifelong Cowboys fan who loved to travel and crack jokes, had visited AT&T Stadium at least two or three times before Sunday, DeLara said. “He just loved the team,” she said. Narro’s niece, Catalina Jenkins, added that she believes her uncle would still be alive “if it weren’t for this football game.” “I just want it to be clear he was an angel of a man, never hurt anyone, never had anything bad to say about anyone,” Jenkins said. “He was so loved. And I’m so sad he fell victim to such mindless violence.” California Post News: Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , X , YouTube , WhatsApp , LinkedIn California Post Sports Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , YouTube , X California Post App: Download here! That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! away.headline: Bengals QB Joe Burrow needs just 2 words to put minds at ease after practicing under the weather
away.blurb: Quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was a full participant once again at practice. He spoke to reporters afterwards and confirmed he'll be good to go for Monday. “For sure,” Burrow said when asked if he'll be at full strength for game day. He also said he likes spicy food when he's under the weather. Good to know. Burrow also mentioned the energy was a bit down around the locker room earlier in the week due to others dealing with sickness. Cornerback Dax Hill is one of them, and he remains out of practice. He may need to practice Saturday or else he's in jeopardy of missing Monday night. Offensive tackle Myles Hinton, the third Bengal listed with an illness, was a full participant again. Linebacker Oren Burks (groin) and right guard Dalton Risner (knee) were the only other DNPs as they were yesterday. Burks isn't expected to practice all week, and Risner was labeled as day-to-day according to coach Zac Taylor to start the week of practice. Left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) was limited, so two of Cincy's starting interior offensive linemen enter the weekend still battling injuries. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) was a full participant in practice for the first time since Week 7. Dugger has been week-to-week for the last few weeks as he's still dealing with an injury from all the way back in Week 3. He looks to have a great shot at returning this weekend. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm), CB Jalen Davis (hamstring), wide receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb), and G Brian Parker II (knee) remain full participants as they await activation to the 53-man roster. Bozeman was designated to return Thursday while the other three were designated to return last week . away.blurb: The opening injury report for Commanders Week just dropped from the Bengals . Guard Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice, as fans hope to see him get a session in over the next two days. Joe Burrow was a full participant with his illness so that should quell any fear he may miss Monday's game. Dax Hill is also dealing with an illness. Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged a limited showing after his injury on Sunday night. Outside of those names, there aren't many big ones to discuss. Cincinnati should get back Andrei Iosivas, Brian Parker and Jalen Davis this week after all three logged full Thursday sessions. Backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) logged a limited session as a nice sign of improvement. A few other special-team names popped up with illnesses but what looks like a big injury list should end up thinning out across the next few days. "Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about Drew Sample and Chase Brown. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out." "We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are." Burks isn't expected to practice all week, while Risner is considered day-to-day. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) and left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) were each limited Thursday. Dugger has been week-to-week for the last few weeks as he's still dealing with an injury from all the way back in Week 3. Fairchild suffered his injury in Week 9 and was able to play most of last week despite it. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) practice for the first time since Week 5 as he was designated to return off the Reserve/Injured list Thursday. Cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring), WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb), and G Brian Parker II (knee) remain full participants as they await activation to the 53-man roster . Bengals' Thursday injury report for NFL Week 11 Joe Burrow isn't alone under the weather Quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was a full participant at practice, but the club announced during practice he is dealing with an illness and would not speak with reporters after practice. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took Burrow's place at his post-practice presser. “I don't know if he told y'all how he's feeling or not, but overall he looks good,” Chase said of Burrow while wearing his orange No. 9 practice jersey. “I think everybody around the team is just coming on with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good. Still feels the same.” He's not wrong. Starting cornerback Dax Hill and offensive tackle Myles Hinton are also dealing with illnesses. Hill wasn't able to practice at all. Hinton was a late add to last week's injury report with his illness and was a full participant Thursday. Burrow being able to practice fully Thursday is obviously good news for his prospects playing Monday. He's expected to address the media either Friday or Saturday.
